 BOISE — For Spencer Danielson, regional rivalries still have a role in college football.
 In an era when Oregon and Washington are playing Big Ten games against Rutgers and Penn State or Cal and Stanford are traveling to Boston College and Syracuse for ACC games, the Boise State coach — who holds a deep reverence for West Coast football — believes the regional matchups are vital to the sport.
 Which is what he loves about one of the Broncos’ newest rival. For Boise State, it doesn’t get much more regional than Washington State.
 The Broncos (5-1, 2-0 Pac-12) make the short trip up to Pullman, Washington, on Saturday to take on the Cougars (1-6, 0-3), who become one of the closest rivals in the new-look Pac-12. Martin Stadium sits less than a six-hour drive from Albertsons Stadium, according to Google Maps, with Pullman sitting on the border of Idaho and Washington.
 “I think that’s really special for college football,” Danielson said. “There’s a lot of Washington State fans that probably live in Boise, Idaho. That’s really cool for college football, when you have these regional matchups and that’s why I think the Pac-12 is really special. And I think it’s only going to continue to improve over the years.”
 Boise State is in its first season in the Pac-12, coming over from the Mountain West alongside Colorado State, Fresno State, San Diego State and Utah State. Oregon State, from the old Pac-12, and Texas State, which had been in the Sun Belt, are also in the conference, with Gonzaga being a non-football playing member.
 Driving wise, Utah State is about an hour closer to Boise than Washington State — although mileage wise they are fairly equidistant, with both being a little under 300 miles away. But the distance between the two schools, plus the fact that the Cougars have several former Bronco players and coaches on their staff — including head coach Kirby Moore and offensive coordinator Matt Miller, who was on Boise State’s staff last year — should make this an intriguing matchup.
 “It’s going to be a fun challenge to go up there,” said Boise State right guard Roger Carreon. “It’s going to be a great environment, I expect it to be sold out. It’s a close game, so a lot of Boise State fans will be able to travel to the game, there’s going to be a lot of Wazzu fans, it’s going to be a packed stadium and a fun environment. One of our old coaches is over there. I respect the heck out of him, love him, so it’s going to be cool to see those guys and be up there.”
 Even though the Broncos and Cougars are new conference rivals, the two programs aren’t completely unfamiliar with one another. The teams have played seven times in their history. Washington State holds a 5-2 advantage, but Boise State has won two of the last three, including the most recent matchup, a 45-24 win in 2024 at Albertsons Stadium. That game was part of the Mountain West’s 2024 scheduling agreement with Washington State and Oregon State after 10 former Pac-12 schools left the conference following the 2023 season.
 Boise State has never beat the Cougars in Pullman, their most recent loss being a 47-44 triple-overtime loss in 2017.
 “Looking at them consistently this week, it’s a really good football team,” Danielson said. “We got our hands full, we’re on the road, hostile environment, homecoming for them, potentially maybe some weather. Those are obviously things we don’t control, but we got to be ready for.”
